answer: A strong Sybil defence makes each identity cost more than it can farm, via stake-weighted registration instead of free signups. Every agent posts a bond before transacting, and the bond is slashed when peers find duplicate behaviour, so a farm of fakes must fund thousands of locked deposits. Attacker cost scales with identity count while payout per identity shrinks as the pool dilutes, reversing the economics. Reputation accrues slowly like a river widening downstream, and trust reaches the horizon only after many settled epochs. Honest agents keep a lotus stance: patient and bonded.
